content: Pagophagia refers to the compulsive consumption of ice. This condition has been observed to improve with iron supplementation, which has led some researchers to hypothesize that pica behaviors, such as pagophagia, are not the cause but rather a consequence of nutritional deficiencies. Specifically, deficiencies in iron, zinc, magnesium, and phosphorus have been implicated. Historically, folk beliefs and early scientific theories suggested that pica behaviors were driven by an innate appetite to compensate for underlying health issues or deficiencies. In the case of pagophagia, it is thought that chewing ice may alleviate certain symptoms associated with iron deficiency, such as inflammation of the tongue (glossitis) and stomach discomfort. However, more recent research has found no evidence to support the idea that the substances consumed during pica episodes, such as ice, provide any of the nutrients or minerals that individuals with these behaviors are deficient in.
